## Objective
Build the playable game page on top of the pure logic module `src/game.js`: a canvas board, score and best score, start/pause/restart flow, keyboard and swipe controls, and a speed ramp. After this task, running `npm start` and opening http://localhost:8000 shows a working Snake game. Rules live entirely in `src/game.js`; this task only draws state, forwards input and drives the tick timer.

## Interface
`src/game.js` is a contract (currently a stub whose functions throw; another task replaces it in parallel). Import only these names from it, exactly as documented in the stub:
`createGame(options?, rng?)`, `turn(state, dir)`, `step(state, rng?)`, `tickMs(score)`, with `GameState` having `cols`, `rows`, `snake`, `food`, `score`, `status` (`'running' | 'over' | 'won'`). Call `createGame()` with no arguments (20x20 board) and `step(state)` with no rng.

Files to create:
- `index.html`: contains exactly these hooks (ids are used by `src/main.js` and checked by verification):
  - `<link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">`
  - `<canvas id="board" width="480" height="480"></canvas>` inside a relatively positioned wrapper, with `<div id="overlay">` containing `<h2 id="overlay-title">` and `<p id="overlay-hint">` placed over the canvas in the same wrapper
  - `<span id="score">0</span>` and `<span id="best">0</span>` in a header above the board
  - a short controls help line below the board
  - `<script type="module" src="src/main.js"></script>` (written exactly with `type="module" src="src/main.js"` in that order)
- `style.css`: dark theme, board centred, overlay covering the canvas with a semi-transparent background and centred text, canvas scales down on narrow screens via CSS width (`max-width: 100%`, `height: auto`) without changing its internal 480x480 resolution, `touch-action: none` on the canvas.
- `src/render.js`: `export function drawBoard(ctx, state, cellSize)`. It clears and paints the whole board each call: background (a subtle checkerboard or grid), the food (a circle, in a contrasting colour), the snake (rounded or inset rectangles; the head in a visibly different shade than the body). It reads only its arguments and touches no DOM or globals.
- `src/main.js`: imports `{ createGame, turn, step, tickMs }` from `'./game.js'` and `{ drawBoard }` from `'./render.js'`; wires everything. Cell size is `canvas.width / state.cols`.
- `README.md`: what the game is, how to run it (`npm start`, then open http://localhost:8000; opening `index.html` via `file://` does not work because browsers block ES modules there), controls, how to run tests (`npm test`), and a three-line file layout (`src/game.js` rules, `src/render.js` drawing, `src/main.js` input and loop).

## Behavior
1. On load `main.js` creates a game, draws it, shows the overlay with title `Snake` and hint `Press an arrow key, WASD or Space to start`, and sets `#score` to 0. The best score is read from `localStorage` key `snake.best` (a missing, invalid or inaccessible value counts as 0) and shown in `#best`. The UI phase is one of `ready`, `playing`, `paused`, `ended`.
2. Direction keys are ArrowUp/ArrowDown/ArrowLeft/ArrowRight and w/a/s/d (case-insensitive), mapped to `'up' | 'down' | 'left' | 'right'`. In `playing` they call `turn(state, dir)` and keep its result. In `ready` they call `turn` and then start the game (phase `playing`, overlay hidden, tick loop started). In `paused` and `ended` they are ignored.
3. Space and Enter share one action: `ready` starts the game; `playing` pauses (overlay shows title `Paused`, hint `Press Space to resume`); `paused` resumes (overlay hidden); `ended` begins a brand-new game immediately (`createGame()`, score display reset to 0, phase `playing`, overlay hidden).
4. The tick loop is a `setTimeout` chain, not `setInterval`. Each tick does `state = step(state)`, redraws with `drawBoard`, and updates `#score`. If `state.status` is still `'running'` it schedules the next tick after `tickMs(state.score)` ms, so the game speeds up as the score grows. Pausing or ending clears the pending timer. At most one timer exists at any time.
5. When `step` returns status `'over'` or `'won'`: the phase becomes `ended`; the overlay title is `Game over` for `'over'` and `You win!` for `'won'`; the hint is `Score: N - press Space to play again` with N the final score; if the score beats the best, update `#best` and persist it to `localStorage` key `snake.best`. The final board stays drawn behind the overlay.
6. Key handling calls `event.preventDefault()` for every key it handles (arrows, WASD, Space, Enter) so the page never scrolls. Events with `ctrlKey`, `metaKey` or `altKey` set are ignored entirely and not prevented. For Space and Enter, events with `event.repeat === true` are ignored so holding the key does not toggle pause repeatedly.
7. When the document becomes hidden (`visibilitychange`) while the phase is `playing`, the game pauses exactly as in behaviour 3.
8. Touch: on the canvas, `touchstart` records the start point and `touchend` computes the delta. If the larger absolute delta is at least 24 px, the dominant axis picks the direction (positive x is right, positive y is down) and it is handled exactly like the matching direction key from behaviour 2. A shorter movement counts as a tap and is handled like Space. The canvas touch listeners are registered with `{ passive: false }` and call `preventDefault()` on touch events they handle.
9. Rendering: `drawBoard(ctx, state, cellSize)` is called once on load, after every tick, and after a restart. A turn alone does not need a redraw, because turns only take effect on the next tick.
10. The code is split into small functions (for example `startGame`, `pauseGame`, `resumeGame`, `endGame`, `handleDirection`, `handleAction`, `tick`, `render`, `showOverlay`, `hideOverlay`), with shared key and touch paths calling the same two handlers `handleDirection(dir)` and `handleAction()`.

## Invariants
- No third-party code, CDN link, web font or build step; everything works from plain static files served by `python3 -m http.server`.
- All game rules (collision, growth, scoring, queueing turns, win) stay in `src/game.js`. Do not reimplement or duplicate any of them; do not keep your own turn queue.
- `src/render.js` has no side effects beyond drawing on the provided context.
- Match the style of `src/game.js`: ES modules, `const`/`let`, semicolons, single quotes, JSDoc where it clarifies a signature.

## Edge cases
- `localStorage` may throw (private mode, disabled storage): wrap every access in `try/catch` and continue with an in-memory best score.
- Resuming from pause must not create a second timer (clear any existing timer before scheduling).
- Starting from `ready` by pressing ArrowLeft: the reversal is ignored by `turn`, the game must still start and move right.
- Restart after `ended` must discard the old state completely, including resetting `#score` and redrawing.
- CSS trap: `#overlay` uses a `display` value that overrides the `hidden` attribute, so the stylesheet must include `#overlay[hidden] { display: none; }` and `hideOverlay` should set the `hidden` attribute.

## Guardrails
- Do not modify `src/game.js`, `package.json` or anything under `test/`; do not add a UI test file or any dependency.
- Do not import any name from `./game.js` other than `createGame`, `turn`, `step`, `tickMs`; verification checks every imported name exists.
- Do not use inline event handler attributes in HTML, and do not write inline `<script>` code or inline `<style>` blocks.
- The grep check in verification matches the exact markup strings given above: keep `id="board"`, `id="score"`, `id="best"`, `id="overlay"`, `id="overlay-title"`, `id="overlay-hint"`, `href="style.css"` and `type="module" src="src/main.js"` verbatim.

## Out of scope
Game rules and tests (tasks T1 and T2), sound, difficulty settings, a leaderboard, obstacles, wrap-around walls, mobile on-screen buttons, and any packaging or deployment.
